newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Former rebel chief takes office in Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Former rebel chief takes office in Philippines.

text.p: The former rebel chief who led a bloody war for Moslem independence in the southern Philippines took office as regional governor on Monday, vowing to turn his battered homeland into an economic growth area.

"We have had too much of bloodhshed in this land... We must stop it once and for all," Nur Misuari said after President Fidel Ramos installed him as head of a semi-autonomous region comprising four impoverished Moslem provinces.

At the swearing-in ceremony, Ramos beat a native Moslem gong three times to complete the return to the national mainstream of the guerrilla leader who plunged the country into 24 years of civil war that killed more than 120,000 people.

Ramos had earlier held up his government's peace deal with Misuari's guerrillas as an example to Israelis and Palestinians that "living as neighbours requires...tolerance and consideration of each other's interests at all times."

Misuari, the 55-year-old chief of the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) signed a peace settlement with Manila on September 2 and was elected regional governor a week later after running unopposed as the administration's candidate.

As part of the deal, Ramos was expected to name Misuari to a second post this week as head of a council to oversee the development of 14 southern provinces and nine cities in the Mindanao region, most of which are dominated by Christians.

Ramos appealed to Christian politicians fiercely opposed to the deal "to give peace a chance," saying Misuar's return to the fold would bolster political stability and open up largely underdeveloped Mindanao to foreign investments.
Ramos and Misuari spoke at an open air ceremony in Cotabato city attended by about 20,000 people, including diplomats from Islamic nations and some 15,000 unarmed MNLF fighters.
Misuari, a former political science teacher at University of the Philippines, said his installation as governor marked his "break with the past."
"We have made our intention clear and unmistakeable, that we are now about to burn our bridges to armed struggle or armed jihad," he said.

He urged all Moslems and Christians to help fulfil the economic promise of timber- and mineral-rich Mindanao, seen as a future hub of the East Asian Growth Area that comprises underdeveloped areas of Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines.
"All our people in this region, except for the lazy ones, shall become participants and new warriors for this war against backwardness, poverty (and) lawlessness," Misuari said.

Ramos, who has committed $1.2 billion in aid to Misuari for next year, promised to build roads, seaports, airports, power plants and telecommunications facilities in the semi-autonomous area comprising the provinces of Maguindanao, Lanao del Sur, Tawi-Tawi and Sulu.
The area, regarded as among the poorest in the country, has a population of 2.1 million, 97 percent of them Moslem.

The proposed 14-province development council Misuari will head will be the forerunner of an expanded autonomy area to be created three years from now and to comprise provinces, whether Moslem or Christian, that vote to join it in a plebiscite.
